relationships.subject: TrkB
relationships.evidence_quote: Similar to EphB2 and NMDARs, TrkB activates Tiam1 [68,69] and Rac1-dependent spine remodelling [70].

relationships.subject: EphB2
relationships.evidence_quote: EphB2 can also signal to individual Rho-GTPases via multiple GEFs: for instance, it activates Rac1 by the Rac1-GEF Kalirin-7 in addition to Tiam1 [58].

relationships.subject: Bcr
relationships.evidence_quote: Tiam1/Bcr complex disruption results in overactive Rac1, increased spine density and size, and converts a spinogenic ephrin-B/EphB2 signal into spine loss [50].

relationships.subject: BDNF
relationships.evidence_quote: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and its receptor TrkB also regulate spine formation and function [67].

key_findings: Review: Rho-GTPases (RhoA, Rac1, Cdc42) are regulated by GEFs/GAPs downstream of EphB2, NMDAR and BDNF-TrkB to control spine morphology.
Rac1 and Cdc42 promote growth and synaptic strength while RhoA opposes it.
